card.name: Words just before a past 'once' or 'used to'
card.fires_on: The word right before an expected 'once', 'used to' or 'time' that refers to a former state, such as 'At one', 'as it', 'than we' or 'where Jews'. It appears in general web text about how things used to be.

modes.label: At one (time)
modes.description: The word 'one' in 'At one time' opening a sentence about the past.
modes.example: At<< one>> time garden chemicals were championed as the

modes.label: Pronoun before once/used to
modes.description: A pronoun or verb in a comparison clause where 'once' or 'used to' is expected next.
modes.example: as<< it>> once did. The palace was damaged by

modes.label: Past-place clause
modes.description: A subject word in a clause about a former situation, where 'once' could follow.
modes.example: now mark pathways where<< Jews>> walked for centuries.

card.writes: It pushes the model to predict 'once' next and holds back 'today' and similar present-time words.
card.plain: It fires on the word just before 'once' or 'used to' when the text describes how things were in the past.
